quizzes.title: Western Ghats and Space Science
quizzes.passage: Ecologically Sensitive Areas are zones that the government can notify to protect the natural environment. Once an area is notified, activities that could harm its ecology are regulated, with the aim of conserving biodiversity, forests, wildlife habitats and water resources. Such areas can include forests, biodiversity hotspots, rivers, hills and wetlands. These regions are notified by the environment ministry under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and the process moves in stages. The Western Ghats, a long range of hills along India's west coast, have been the subject of such a proposal for many years, and the notification is now being prepared. Recommendations made earlier have shaped the proposal. Within these areas, sustainable livelihoods, eco-tourism, traditional agriculture and conservation-based practices are generally allowed. Environmental rules can restrict some heavy-impact activities while leaving room for practices that are less damaging to the land. Space science also draws attention in India. Scientists use ground-based observatories to study particles that arrive from outer space, and collaborations between research teams help them follow changes in the planet's atmosphere. Meanwhile, international reports measure how countries are moving toward energy systems that are secure, sustainable, equitable and affordable. These developments show how environmental protection, scientific research and energy planning appear together in current affairs.

questions.q: Which committee's 2013 recommendations form the basis of the government's proposed notification of Ecologically Sensitive Areas in the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The notification is based largely on the K. Kasturirangan Committee's 2013 recommendations.

questions.q: The Kasturirangan approach covers roughly what share of the Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The approach covers about 56,000 sq km, which is about 37% of the Western Ghats.

questions.q: Which institution operates the GRAPES-3 cosmic-ray observatory?
questions.explanation: GRAPES-3 is operated by the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Western Ghats are known as the 'Water Tower of Peninsular India'.
Reason (R): The Western Ghats are the source of major rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The named rivers are the reason the range is called the Water Tower of Peninsular India.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Anamudi   ->   B. Also known as the Sahyadri Range
II. GRAPES-3   ->   D. Highest peak of the range, located in Kerala
III. Energy Transition Index 2026   ->   C. Cosmic-ray observatory at Ooty
IV. Western Ghats   ->   A. Assessment of 120 countries
questions.explanation: Anamudi is the highest peak, GRAPES-3 is at Ooty, the Energy Transition Index assesses 120 countries, and the Western Ghats are also called the Sahyadri Range.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ecologically Sensitive Areas:
I. The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
II. Organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted activities in these areas.
III. All large construction projects are permitted in these areas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Large construction projects are restricted in these areas, so statement III is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Western Ghats:
I. The range extends about 1,600 km along India's west coast.
II. The range spans eight states.
III. New thermal power plants are restricted in Ecologically Sensitive Areas.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the range spans six states, not eight.

quizzes.title: Western Ghats and GRAPES-3 Facts
quizzes.passage: The Western Ghats run along India's west coast and are home to rich forests and many species. The government plans to notify Ecologically Sensitive Areas across this range, a step that has been pending for a long time. A draft notification comes before the final one, and such areas can include biodiversity hotspots, wetlands, hills and rivers. Such areas are meant to regulate activities that could damage the environment, so that biodiversity, forests, wildlife habitats, water resources and ecological connectivity are protected. Restrictions apply to some heavy industrial and mining projects, while low-impact practices such as organic farming, rainwater harvesting and eco-tourism remain permitted. In space science, a cosmic-ray observatory in southern India has been used by scientists from more than one country to study the upper atmosphere in near real time. The basic objective of that observatory is to understand the origin, acceleration and propagation of cosmic rays. Such research helps scientists understand how particles from outer space behave. In the field of energy, a global assessment rates countries on how well they are shifting towards systems that are secure, sustainable, equitable and affordable. The assessment covers a large group of nations and offers a yearly snapshot of progress. Together, these topics show the range of environmental, scientific and energy issues in current affairs.

questions.q: Which Indian state hosts the GRAPES-3 cosmic-ray observatory?
questions.explanation: GRAPES-3 is located at Ooty in Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Approximately how long, in km, does the Western Ghats extend along India's west coast?
questions.explanation: The range extends about 1,600 km along the west coast.

questions.q: What is the name of the highest peak in the Western Ghats, located in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Anamudi in Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.

questions.q: In which year was the Environment (Protection) Act enacted, under which ecologically fragile regions are notified?
questions.explanation: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986.

questions.q: Across how many states does the Western Ghats extend?
questions.explanation: The range spans six states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Researchers from which country joined India in using GRAPES-3 to track changes in Earth's upper atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Researchers from India and Japan used GRAPES-3 for this study.

questions.q: Which organisation publishes the Energy Transition Index together with Accenture?
questions.explanation: The Energy Transition Index 2026 is published by the World Economic Forum and Accenture.

quizzes.title: FCRA Rules and Global Bodies
quizzes.passage: The Ministry of Home Affairs has notified new rules for non-governmental organisations that receive contributions from abroad. The rules aim at stricter compliance, transparency and monitoring, and they operate under a law meant to protect India's sovereignty, integrity, security and national interest. Organisations seeking such funds must have their activities placed under defined categories, and they must disclose details about their work, the states where they operate and their public outreach. Certain persons in leadership roles are also covered, as the rules widen the definition of who manages an organisation. Funds are linked to utilisation as well, so an organisation's record of spending earlier money affects whether it receives more. The governing law is also meant to stop foreign money from being used for religious conversion. Separately, an intergovernmental body works against money laundering and the financing of terrorism, and its lists of countries under scrutiny carry different implications for access to financial markets. India also takes part in United Nations peacekeeping, where troops and police are deployed to regions affected by conflict or political instability. Such missions have been recognised with a Nobel Peace Prize, and their personnel are often called Blue Helmets. The broader picture shows how domestic regulation and global cooperation both shape the way resources and peace efforts move across borders.

questions.q: NGOs must utilise at least what share of previously released foreign funds before receiving the next instalment?
questions.explanation: Under the FCRA Amendment Rules 2026, at least 75% of previously released foreign funds must be used before the next instalment.

questions.q: For how long is an FCRA registration valid before it must be renewed?
questions.explanation: FCRA registration is valid for five years and must be renewed before expiry.

questions.q: Which grouping of countries created the Financial Action Task Force in 1989?
questions.explanation: FATF was created in 1989 by the Group of Seven (G7).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Foreign contributions cannot be passed on to other persons or organisations.
Reason (R): The FCRA (Amendment) Act 2020 prohibits transfer or sub-granting of foreign contributions to any other person or organisation.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The 2020 Act's prohibition on transfer is the reason foreign contributions cannot be passed on.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Grey List   ->   D. Calls for protecting women and girls from conflict-related sexual violence
II. Black List   ->   A. US-led initiative for secure AI-critical supply chains
III. Pax Silica   ->   B. Jurisdictions under increased monitoring
IV. Principles of the 2000 UN Security Council Resolution   ->   C. High-risk jurisdictions
questions.explanation: The Grey List covers jurisdictions under increased monitoring, the Black List covers high-risk jurisdictions, Pax Silica is a US-led supply chain initiative, and the 2000 resolution calls for protecting women and girls from conflict-related sexual violence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Vivek Aggarwal has been appointed as the next Vice-President of the FATF, the first time India will hold that post.
II. The FCRA Act, 2010 replaced the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976.
III. NGOs with any foreign national as a key functionary are automatically eligible for FCRA registration.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is false because foreign nationals other than Persons of Indian Origin as key functionaries ordinarily make an NGO ineligible.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India joined the Pax Silica initiative in February 2026.
II. The International Day of UN Peacekeepers is observed on 24 October.
III. India was the first country to deploy an all-women contingent to a UN peacekeeping mission.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the peacekeepers' day is observed on 29 May.

quizzes.title: FCRA, FATF and Peacekeeping Facts
quizzes.passage: The Ministry of Home Affairs has notified amended rules that tighten compliance for non-governmental organisations receiving money from abroad. Under the governing law, such organisations must register under approved categories, disclose their activities and public materials, and renew their registration before it expires. Registration certificates must specify the purposes and the states or union territories where activities will be carried out. Funds from overseas must first arrive in a designated account at a public sector bank, and they cannot be passed on to other bodies. Other parts of the rules deal with who may hold key roles in an organisation and how spending must be reported. Foreign contributions may be used for religious worship, religious education and community kitchens, but not for religious conversion. Separately, a body based in Europe works on combating money laundering and the financing of terrorism, and it publishes lists of jurisdictions whose systems have weaknesses. The United Nations also runs peacekeeping missions, which involve military, police and civilian personnel. Each year a day is observed in honour of peacekeepers, and the theme for 2026 focuses on investing in peace. Recognition also goes to peacekeepers who work on gender issues in missions, reflecting principles adopted by the UN Security Council to protect women and girls in conflict zones.

questions.q: In which year was the FCRA Act that replaced the 1976 law enacted?
questions.explanation: The FCRA Act was enacted in 2010, replacing the 1976 Act.

questions.q: How many approved categories must an NGO register under at least one of?
questions.explanation: NGOs must register under one or more of five approved categories: social, economic, educational, cultural and religious.

questions.q: In which city is the designated FCRA account at the State Bank of India's main branch located?
questions.explanation: All foreign contributions must first be received in the designated FCRA account at the SBI main branch in New Delhi.

questions.q: In which city is the headquarters of the Financial Action Task Force located?
questions.explanation: FATF is headquartered in Paris, France.

questions.q: Which US-led initiative for secure supply chains of AI-critical technologies did India join in February 2026?
questions.explanation: India joined Pax Silica in February 2026 during the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi.

questions.q: On which date is the International Day of UN Peacekeepers observed each year? (day and month)
questions.explanation: The International Day of UN Peacekeepers is observed on 29 May.

questions.q: Which Indian officer received the UN Military Gender Advocate of the Year Award 2025 for work in UNIFIL, Lebanon?
questions.explanation: Major Abhilasha Barak received the award for advancing gender equality in peacekeeping missions in Lebanon.

quizzes.title: Padma Awards and University Rankings
quizzes.passage: India's civilian honours recognise achievement across many fields, and the President confers them at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The Padma honours are among the best known of these, and they are given after a multi-stage process. The Padma Vibhushan is India's second highest civilian honour, after the Bharat Ratna. Recommendations come from a committee, the proposals are reviewed at the top level of government, and the final approval rests with the head of state. The Constitution abolishes titles, but the Supreme Court has upheld the Padma honours as recognition of merit and public service rather than as titles, and recipients may not use them as prefixes or suffixes to their names. Government servants are generally not eligible, though doctors and scientists are an exception. The government also honours children each year for achievements in fields such as bravery, innovation and sports, through an award presented at Vigyan Bhawan. University rankings attract similar attention. Such rankings are built on several parameters, including reputation among academics and employers, research output and the share of international students and faculty. The methodology weighs each parameter, so the total score depends on how each parameter is weighted. Both subjects appear in the same part of the current affairs coverage.

questions.q: What is the annual maximum number of Padma Awards that may be conferred?
questions.explanation: The maximum is 120 awards per year, and the cap excludes posthumous awards and some other categories of recipients.

questions.q: In which year were the Padma Awards instituted?
questions.explanation: The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and reorganised in 1955.

questions.q: The PM Rashtriya Bal Puraskar was created in 2018 by merging which two earlier awards?
options: Bal Kalyan Puraskar and Bal Shakti Puraskar
Bal Shakti Puraskar and Padma Shri
questions.explanation: The PM Rashtriya Bal Puraskar was created in 2018 by merging the Bal Kalyan Puraskar and the Bal Shakti Puraskar.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Foreign nationals are ineligible for Padma Awards.
Reason (R): Foreign nationals are excluded from the annual cap on Padma Awards.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Foreign nationals are listed as eligible for Padma Awards, but they are excluded from the cap, so A is false and R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Padma Vibhushan   ->   D. Children aged 5 to 18
II. Padma Bhushan   ->   A. Exceptional and distinguished service of the highest order
III. Padma Shri   ->   B. Distinguished service of a high order in any field
IV. PM Rashtriya Bal Puraskar   ->   C. Distinguished contributions and achievements in any discipline or area of public life
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan is for exceptional service of the highest order, Padma Bhushan for high-order service in any field, Padma Shri for contributions in any discipline, and the PM Bal Puraskar is for children aged 5 to 18.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Padma Awards:
I. The Padma Awards selection committee is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.
II. Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Independence Day.
III. A recipient normally needs at least five years to elapse before being considered for a higher Padma category.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Awards are announced on the eve of Republic Day, so statement II is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about QS World University Rankings 2027:
I. The rankings were released by Quacquarelli Symonds.
II. Academic Reputation carries a weight of 30% in the ranking methodology.
III. Employer Reputation carries a weight of 25% in the ranking methodology.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while Employer Reputation carries a weight of 15%.

quizzes.title: Heritage, Health and Yoga Facts
quizzes.passage: The Indus Valley Civilisation has left artefacts that continue to draw public attention. One bronze statuette, showing a young woman standing with one hand on her hip, was shown in a school textbook in a changed form before its original image was restored after criticism. It is estimated to be nearly 4,500 years old, and it was made using the lost-wax casting technique. The figurine shows a young female figure standing confidently, wearing a necklace and numerous bangles, and the civilisation it comes from was one of the most prominent urban centres of its era. The statuette is now housed in a national museum in the capital. Heritage also features in cultural cooperation: two countries are preparing a joint proposal to recognise an ancient travel account on a documentary heritage list. That account describes journeys across India and Central Asia during the seventh century CE. In health, a national survey collects data on fertility, nutrition and immunisation, and its latest round reports rising institutional deliveries and lower stunting among children. Yoga is promoted through an annual international observance that coincides with the summer solstice, and the United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution to declare the day. Together, these topics show the variety of heritage, health and cultural issues in current affairs.

questions.q: In which year was the first International Day of Yoga observed?
questions.explanation: The first International Day of Yoga was observed in 2015.

questions.q: Into how many categories were the Padma Awards reorganised in 1955?
questions.explanation: The Padma Awards were reorganised in 1955 into three distinct categories.

questions.q: From which Indus Valley city was the bronze Dancing Girl figurine excavated?
questions.explanation: The Dancing Girl figurine was excavated from Mohenjo-daro in 1926.

questions.q: Which archaeologist excavated the Dancing Girl figurine in 1926?
questions.explanation: The figurine was excavated in 1926 by archaeologist Ernest Mackay.

questions.q: Which ministry coordinates the International Day of Yoga activities?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Ayush coordinates and promotes International Day of Yoga activities.

questions.q: What is the theme of International Day of Yoga 2026?
questions.explanation: The 2026 theme was Yoga for Healthy Ageing.

questions.q: In which Indian city was the 2nd BRICS Culture Working Group Meeting held, where the Xuanzang nomination idea emerged?
questions.explanation: The idea of the joint UNESCO nomination emerged during the 2nd BRICS Culture Working Group Meeting in Varanasi.
